identity.name: Inner Mongolia
native_names: 内蒙古自治政府 (Nèi Měnggǔ zìzhì zhèngfǔ)

land.text: the Chahar, Xilingol and Siziwang areas of the 1945 Inner Mongolian People's Republic (9 September to 6 November 1945), whose provisional government Ulanhu dissolved in October 1945 before launching the autonomy movement

predecessors.note: The zh page: Ulanhu dissolved the Provisional Government of the Inner Mongolian People's Republic led by Boyinda'lai in October 1945 and launched the autonomy movement. The Inner Mongolian People's Republic page dates that republic 9 September to 6 November 1945. It has no dossier; the compiled map treats its land as nobody's.

land.text: the Xing'an and Hulunbuir lands of Manchukuo, which the Soviet and Mongolian forces occupied in 1945

predecessors.note: The zh page: late in the war Soviet and Mongolian People's Republic forces occupied all of Eastern Mongolia (undated). Mengjiang (Xilingol, Chahar) and Manchukuo (Xing'an, Hulunbuir) both ended in August 1945 (their dossiers).

land.text: the five leagues of 1947 (Hulunbuir, Nanwenmuren, Hinggan, Xilin Gol and Chahar), '34 banners and cities and 1 county', 538,000 km2 and about 2 million people: Hulunbuir together with the Nanwenmuren league (whose province office stood at Zhalantun, inside the gazetteer's Hulunbuir region), the Hinggan league round Wangyemiao (Ulanhot), and the Xilin Gol and Chahar steppe round Xilinhot; the Jerim league round Tongliao is not among the five the page lists

successors.note: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (established 1947) goes on inside the People's Republic of 1 October 1949 and 'was expanded westwards to include five of the six original leagues' over the next decade (Inner Mongolia page); no page opened dates the expansion or the 1954 merger with Suiyuan.

capitals.name: Wangyemiao (Ulanhot)
capitals.note: The zh page: the people's representative conference of 23 April 1947 was held at Wangyemiao (王爷庙), the modern Ulanhot (gazetteer: Ulan Hot). The page names no capital and no move to Zhangjiakou or Hohhot before October 1949; coordinates are the gazetteer's Ulan Hot.

rulers.name: Ulanhu
rulers.title: Chairman
rulers.note: 'Ulanhu was elected chairman of the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government, Hafeng'a vice-chairman' (zh page, 1947); the Ulanhu page: 'founding Chairman of China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, serving from 1947 to 1966'.

correction.text: the five leagues of 1947 (Hulunbuir, Nanwenmuren, Hinggan, Xilin Gol and Chahar), '34 banners and cities and 1 county', 538,000 km2 and about 2 million people: Hulunbuir together with the Nanwenmuren league (whose province office stood at Zhalantun, inside the gazetteer's Hulunbuir region), the Hinggan league round Wangyemiao (Ulanhot), and the Xilin Gol and Chahar steppe round Xilinhot; the Jerim league round Tongliao is not among the five the page lists

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria shape; in Cliopatria's 1947 shapes 2,440 Inner Mongolian cells belong to nobody and from 1948 to the Communist Party of China shape). The zh page gives the government's own figures at its founding: 'five leagues (Hulunbuir, Nanwenmuren, Hinggan, Xilin Gol, Chahar) with 34 banners (cities) and 1 county, 538,000 km2, about 2 million people'; the 2,318-cell (about 586,000 km2) region here is 1.09 times that, within a factor of two. (Repair: the first draft also drew a 150 km disc round Tongliao as 'the Nanwenmuren league'; the zh Nanwenmuren page puts the province office at Zhalantun, inside Hulunbuir, and Tongliao was the seat of the Jerim league (zh 哲里木盟 page: 'in 1947 it moved its seat to Tongliao and belonged to Liaobei Province', 1947年迁驻通辽，属辽北省), which is not one of the five leagues the zh page lists and was under Liaobei, not the Autonomous Government, until Liaobei was abolished in 1949, so the disc is removed, 268 cells.) The same zh Nanwenmuren page: 'On 23 April 1947 the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government was founded, and on 1 May 1947 the Nanwenmuren league government came under its leadership' (1947年5月1日纳文慕仁盟政府归属内蒙古自治政府领导), and on 11 April 1949 the Hulunbuir and Nanwenmuren leagues merged into the Hulunbuir-Nanwenmuren league. The en Inner Mongolia page says 'Initially, the autonomous region included just the Hulunbuir region', which disagrees with the zh page; the zh page is followed because it lists the leagues and the area. The Chahar league is not drawn separately (no gazetteer name for the 1947 league; it overlaps the Communist shape). The shape is unchanged 1947-1949: the pages date no expansion before October 1949. Overlaps the Communist Party of China shape of 1947-1949 (581 cells in 1947), which the compiler must resolve.

region.text: the five leagues of 1947 (Hulunbuir, Nanwenmuren, Hinggan, Xilin Gol and Chahar), '34 banners and cities and 1 county', 538,000 km2 and about 2 million people: Hulunbuir together with the Nanwenmuren league (whose province office stood at Zhalantun, inside the gazetteer's Hulunbuir region), the Hinggan league round Wangyemiao (Ulanhot), and the Xilin Gol and Chahar steppe round Xilinhot; the Jerim league round Tongliao is not among the five the page lists

ledger.note: 1 May 1947: the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government is proclaimed at Wangyemiao with Ulanhu as chairman. 'At the people's representative conference at Wangyemiao on 23 April 1947 ... the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government was proclaimed' and the conference 'set 1 May as the founding anniversary'; 'at its founding it covered the five leagues of Hulunbuir, Nanwenmuren, Hinggan, Xilin Gol and Chahar with 34 banners (cities) and 1 county, 538,000 km2, some 2 million people'. The leagues are the page's; the discs that stand for them are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the five leagues of 1947 (Hulunbuir, Nanwenmuren, Hinggan, Xilin Gol and Chahar), '34 banners and cities and 1 county', 538,000 km2 and about 2 million people: Hulunbuir together with the Nanwenmuren league (whose province office stood at Zhalantun, inside the gazetteer's Hulunbuir region), the Hinggan league round Wangyemiao (Ulanhot), and the Xilin Gol and Chahar steppe round Xilinhot; the Jerim league round Tongliao is not among the five the page lists

ledger.note: 1 October 1949: the Communist-led autonomous government becomes part of the People's Republic. Page silent: the Inner Mongolia page says only that the Communists 'established the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region in 1947' and that it 'was expanded westwards' as 'the communists established the People's Republic of China'; the end date is the proclamation of the People's Republic on 1 October 1949 (the communist-party-of-china ledger), a bridging judgment. Repair round: the zh pages for the region, the Nanwenmuren league and Ulanhu were read again for a dated end and are silent; the zh page on the government itself (内蒙古自治政府) and 内蒙古人民政府 did not load (url_not_found), so the end stays at confidence 1.

certainty.note: The zh page counts leagues, banners and an area but draws no line; the drawn edge follows discs round the leagues' seats and the steppe frontier is soft throughout.

sources.title: 内蒙古自治区 (Chinese Wikipedia, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region)
sources.note: The only page opened that dates and sizes the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government: 23 April 1947 conference at Wangyemiao, Ulanhu chairman, 1 May founding anniversary, five leagues, 34 banners, 538,000 km2, 1945 dissolution of the provisional government. Read in Chinese; quotes are glossed.

sources.title: Inner Mongolian People's Republic
sources.note: 9 September to 6 November 1945; congress in what is now the Sonid Right Banner; Chahar, Xilingol and Siziwang areas; Ulanhu sent to take control. Silent on 1946-1949.

sources.title: Inner Mongolia
sources.note: 'established the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region in 1947', 'Initially, the autonomous region included just the Hulunbuir region', later expansion westwards; silent on the 1 May date and on 1948-1949.

sources.title: Ulanhu
sources.note: Acting Governor and founding Chairman of the Autonomous Government of Inner Mongolia in 1947; chairman of the region 1947 to 1966. Nothing on territory.

sources.title: History of Inner Mongolia
sources.note: Region established in 1947 from the former Suiyuan, Chahar, Rehe, Liaobei and Xing'an provinces; initially only Hulunbuir; Hohhot named capital without a date. Silent on the Civil War in Chahar, Rehe and Suiyuan.

sources.title: Chahar Province
sources.note: Part of Mengjiang 1937-1945; abolished 1952; silent on who held Chahar in 1945-1949 and on Kalgan.

sources.title: Suiyuan
sources.note: Part of Mengjiang 1937-1945; reorganised as a PRC province in 1949; incorporated into the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region in 1954. Silent on Fu Zuoyi and the 1949 handover.

sources.title: Rehe Province
sources.note: Abolished 1955 and divided; silent on 1945-1949 holders and on Chengde.

sources.title: 纳文慕仁盟 (Chinese Wikipedia, Nanwenmuren League)
sources.note: Province office (省公署) at Zhalantun (3 May 1946); league government came under the Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government on 1 May 1947; merged with Hulunbuir on 11 April 1949. Gives Zhalantun, not Tongliao, as the seat. Read in Chinese; quotes are glossed.

sources.title: 乌兰夫 (Chinese Wikipedia, Ulanhu)
sources.note: '1947年5月，乌兰夫又领导组建内蒙古自治政府，并被选为主席' (May 1947: Ulanhu led the founding of the government and was elected chairman); renames of the army in January 1948 and May 1949; silent on any renaming of the government or a move of the capital.

sources.title: 哲里木盟 (Chinese Wikipedia, Jerim League)
sources.note: Jerim league government set up in 1946 at Bayantala, moved its seat to Tongliao in 1947 and belonged to Liaobei Province; Liaobei was abolished in 1949 and its land put under the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (no month given). Read in Chinese; quotes are glossed.

notes: Requested by the p1940-p1949 window (2,430 Inner Mongolian cells nobody's in 1947-48 after the republic-of-china_1947 snap; by Cliopatria's shapes alone, 2,440 cells of the Inner Mongol admin-1 are in no 1947 shape of the Republic of China or the Communist Party of China). The dossier covers the Communist-led Inner Mongolian Autonomous Government of 1947-1949, 'the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region' of the pages, drawn as the five leagues the zh page lists for 1947; a state of the Inner Mongolian autonomous movement is the only candidate the pages opened give. Not settled and left out: (1) the English Chahar, Suiyuan and Rehe pages are silent on who held those provinces in 1945-1949 (no page opened dates who held Chengde, Kalgan, Guisui or Baotou between 1945 and 1949), so Chahar, Suiyuan and Rehe stay with the republic-of-china and communist-party-of-china dossiers; (2) the Zhaowuda league round Chifeng (260 of the 2,440 cells) and about 140 cells in the Alxa and Ejin west are in nobody's land in 1947 and in no league the zh page lists for 1947; (3) 1946, when Cliopatria's shapes leave about 4,200 Inner Mongolian cells with no owner, is before the government existed: the Eastern Mongolian Autonomous Government (1946) and the 1945 Inner Mongolian People's Republic have no dossier and no page opened dates the 1946 holder; (4) the en pages say the government initially held 'just the Hulunbuir region', the zh page five leagues: the zh page is followed. The end year is a bridging judgment (confidence 1): the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region continues inside the PRC; people-s-republic-of-china lists communist-party-of-china and republic-of-china as predecessors but not this slug. The inner-mongolian-people-s-republic predecessor needs a dossier (9 September to 6 November 1945). Gazetteer names needed: Hinggan League and Nanwenmuren League (leagues), Chahar League, Wangyemiao as an alias of Ulan Hot. Pages that did not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_Mongolian_Autonomous_Government and https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%86%85%E8%92%99%E5%8F%A4%E8%87%AA%E6%B2%BB%E6%94%BF%E5%BA%9C (url_not_found). Wikidata id not known. REPAIR ROUND (reviewer's blocking finding): the Tongliao 150 km disc, drawn as the Nanwenmuren league, was a misidentification: the zh Nanwenmuren page puts the province office at Zhalantun (inside the gazetteer's Hulunbuir region, 46 of the 53 cells of a 60 km disc around Zalantun; the other 7 cells are not drawn) and Tongliao was the seat of the Jerim league, which the zh 内蒙古自治区 page does not list among the five leagues of 1947. The disc is removed from the keyframe correction, the found and dissolve regions and the PRC successor land; the region is now 2,318 cells (about 586,000 km2, ratio 1.09 to the page's 538,000). Zhalantun is already in the gazetteer (as an alias of Zalantun), so it is no longer a name needed. Still not settled: the Chahar league is drawn only where the 250 km Xilinhot disc reaches, because no page opened locates it; the end at 1949-10 is a bridging judgment (confidence 1) because no page opened dates it. The zh 哲里木盟 page (opened to check the reviewer's claim) confirms that Tongliao was the Jerim league's seat from 1947 and that the league belonged to Liaobei Province; it dates the entry of that land into Inner Mongolia only as 1949, with no month, so no gain event is booked for it.
